assign.outcome:
**All four Importance defects fixed, each re-pressed headless on the code that ships.** The two screens are `/imagine/importance/` (what matters most here, ranked) and `/imagine/importance/judge/?at=car` (two things, one question).

![](04-after-1280.png)

**4 · the judge cards** now say they are cards you press — one line above the pair (*click the one that matters more, or press its key*) and a labelled strip at each card's foot (*Pick this one · 1 · ←*). Enter in the name or reason field hands the keyboard back, so the keys stop being dead the moment you type your name. [after](04-after-1280.png)

**6 · a caveat page has a way back.** `Graph.up()` followed only the downward relations, and a caveat hangs upward — so it had no trail at all. It reads both directions now, and every name that navigates wears the site's own link underline instead of nothing. [after](06-after-1280.png)

**9 · the picture carries the sentence.** The three-sentence paragraph describing the bar chart under it is deleted; the count beside each bar reads *100% — won 3 of 3*; and the trace control is a labelled row toggle (*Why? Show the 3 judgments* ↔ *Hide the 3 judgments*) instead of the word "why?" at 0.65em. [after](09-after-1280.png)

**10 · the scores are the reward, not the briefing.** A judge card carries no score until you pick; then both appear, the one you chose is marked *you picked this*, and the next pair waits behind *Next two* (or Enter) — so a pick is never a screen that replaced itself. And the big *Which matters more?* is drawn off, with the reason beside it, on any node with fewer than two things to compare. [after](10-after-1280.png)

**Clean** — three test judgments cast by the runs, all three removed by id; the owner's three data files hash byte-identical to the pre-run snapshot (`20ab6e35…` / `cc5bb7bd…` / `9234ba29…`, 4 / 3 / 3 rows). Private server on 8097 killed by pid; port 80 untouched. Nothing committed.

**Controls** — all 14 of the critic's control kinds now carry a label and a consequence you can see in one frame, plus the one new kind (*Next two*): **15 of 15**. The single exception is the rank numeral, kept as a silent second surface for the labelled toggle beside it because the owner asked for "click a rank to see the judgments behind it"; it shares that toggle's `flip()`, so the two can never disagree.

**Left** — the ranked list's controls still sit inside the streamed region `.imp-live`, so another window's judgment closes an open trace. None of them holds typed text, which is what the caret rule protects; splitting the list would cost a second box for no gesture anyone loses.
